# Lucyn

> Lucyn is the institutional memory of your company. It reads the work engineering
> teams already produce — commits, pull requests, meetings, and conversations — and
> turns it into a living, connected map of how the company actually works, then
> answers questions about it in plain English with citations.

Lucyn is currently pre-launch and operating a waitlist.

## What it does

- **Ingests**: Connects to GitHub, Discord, and Google Meet, reading commits, PRs,
  meetings, and conversations continuously.
- **Maps**: Classifies and embeds every signal into a structured knowledge graph
  linking repos, developers, and decisions to the reasoning behind them.
- **Answers**: Responds to plain-English questions about the organization with
  grounded, cited answers — delivery risk, workload balance, code ownership,
  and why past decisions were made.

## Where it runs

- **Leadership**: A dashboard surfacing engineering health, delivery confidence,
  open PRs, and risk signals.
- **Developers**: A Discord bot that assigns and explains work based on demonstrated
  expertise.
- **Full team**: The company brain itself, written as structured Markdown files —
  human-readable, editable, and continuously updated.

## Principles

- **Acts, not reports**: Existing tools analyze data. Lucyn does something with it.
- **Private by design**: Developer data is never shown to managers. Non-punitive, always.
- **Human in the loop**: Every suggestion needs approval. Lucyn recommends, you decide.
- **Gets smarter over time**: The longer it runs, the better it understands the org.
